title: Gyratory Crusher

introduction.definition: A gyratory crusher is a large primary crusher with a long, steep crushing chamber. The main shaft, carrying the mantle, hangs from a spider at the top and is gyrated at the bottom by an eccentric. Large rocks are crushed between the mantle and the concaves lining the shell. It accepts direct truck dumping and has very high capacity.
applications: Primary crushing in large mines and quarries
High-tonnage copper, iron ore and gold operations
key_points: Continuous crushing on all sides of the head
Shaft supported by the top spider
introduction.summary: A gyratory crusher is a large primary crusher. A long main shaft with a mantle hangs from a spider at the top and gyrates inside a tall concave; trucks dump ore straight in, and it crushes continuously around the circle — higher capacity than a jaw crusher.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Capacity rises with open-side setting and throw; product top size ≈ open-side setting.

wear.title: Concave and mantle wear profile
wear.description: Wear is heaviest in the lower (parallel) zone, where the particles are smallest, the gap is closest and the crushing force is concentrated (purple). As the liners wear the closed-side setting opens, so it is re-adjusted (hydraulic or screw adjustment) to hold product size; liners are changed when the profile can no longer hold the setting or capacity drops.

foundation: Mount on a massive reinforced-concrete foundation or steel structure designed for the crusher's dynamic loads (maker's load data); use anti-vibration mounts where specified.
Allow crane access and lay-down space for liner and wear-part changes.
alignment: Align motor and crusher sheaves or coupling; set V-belt tension to the maker's figure.
Set the closed-side setting (CSS) or gap with the maker's gauge/lead-ball method.
piping: Feed with a controlled feeder (choke or regulated feed as designed); avoid segregated or one-sided feed.
Fit a tramp-metal magnet or metal detector ahead of the crusher and dust extraction at transfer points.
Lubrication system: connect oil supply/return, cooler and filter; check flow and pressure switches.
commissioning: Check lubrication flows and temperatures before starting; run empty to check direction, vibration and current.
Introduce feed gradually; measure product size and adjust the setting; record power draw as a baseline.

routine.task: Check oil flow, pressure and temperature; listen for knocking.

periodic.task: Measure CSS and liner wear; adjust setting.

overhaul.task: Replace mantle and concaves; inspect eccentric bushing and gears.

lubrication: Circulating oil system: check filter ΔP, oil analysis, cooler performance.

remedies: Adjust setting; replace liners; distribute feed evenly

symptoms: High oil temperature, low pressure alarm
remedies: Fix system; never run without oil flow

causes: Tramp metal, packing, too small setting
remedies: Remove tramp; increase setting; regulate feed

safety: Lock out; use the maker's lifting tools for the main shaft and spider; manage rock-fall risk at the dump pocket.

video_tutorials.title: Gyratory Crusher — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Gyratory Crusher.
Check oil flow, pressure and temperature; listen for knocking.
Measure CSS and liner wear; adjust setting.
Replace mantle and concaves; inspect eccentric bushing and gears.
Watch for liner wear: product coarsening, falling capacity. Common cause: normal abrasion, uneven feed.
Watch for lubrication failure: high oil temperature, low pressure alarm. Common cause: pump/filter/cooler fault, contaminated oil.
Watch for ring bounce / overload: bowl lifts, loud bangs. Common cause: tramp metal, packing, too small setting.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
